title: The Upside-Down Picnic Map
synopsis: Danny and Kate follow a picture map, notice the pond on the wrong side, and turn the paper around.

related_resources.reason: Open-ended questions can invite children to compare observations; this is not evidence of map-reading competence.
AAP-hosted shared-reading tips invite prediction and noticing; no experimental study of this story.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: But she was holding it upside down.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: A simple mismatch creates a nonthreatening, listener-followable puzzle.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Parent/caregiver guidance supports only broad age-appropriate editorial practices. It does not assess this original story or prove any cognitive, behavioral or sleep outcome.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Kate turned the paper halfway around.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The characters test an explanation by changing one visible feature.

source_note: Original fiction. Parent-facing sources justify only broad shared-reading/play contexts; fictional stars, giants, dragon sneezes, and the narrative outcomes are not findings in cited research. No sleep or developmental gains are claimed.
